answer: In an AI consensus network, the Byzantine Fault Tolerance (BFT) mechanism with voting-based Sybil resistance can be employed. This method involves each agent casting votes on proposals, with proposals requiring a threshold of votes to pass. A fake agent's votes are easily detectable, as they often diverge from the majority, much like a hollow shell lacks the vibrancy of a crystal quartz. Furthermore, the umber-colored noise of a malicious agent's votes can be filtered out by the network, rendering them inconsequential, thus preventing a Sybil attack.
